messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard? version:3.1.0 IP:192.168.11.33 API name: get nodes list Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI"

They want to generate a RESTful API request. They provided IP, API name, parameter. We need to produce the request. The tool function requests_get can be used to send HTTP GET request. We need to call it with URL: "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI" and fabricName: "PEK-ACI". The function expects fabricName param. So we call functions.requests_get with url and fabricName. The default URL includes placeholder. We need to replace placeholder. So we call with url: "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI" and fabricName: "PEK-ACI". Then we return the result. Also we might explain how to generate the request manually. But the user likely wants the request. So we can provide the HTTP GET request details: method, URL, headers (like Authorization, Content-Type). Provide example using curl. Also mention that you need to use HTTPS, maybe with certificate. Provide the function call.

Thus we should respond with the request details and call the function.
